# YellowPages.com Business Listings and Ratings Scraper

YellowPages.com remains one of the largest searchable directories of US local businesses — restaurants, contractors, salons, repair shops and more. This actor turns a keyword-and-location search, a category browse page, or a list of business profile URLs into structured records with contact info, star rating, review count and hours.

## What this actor does

- Searches by keyword plus a city/state or ZIP code, matching YellowPages' own search box
- Browses a specific category-and-location combination using YellowPages' category slugs
- Enriches a known list of business profile URLs directly, skipping the search step entirely
- Sorts results by relevance, distance, rating or name, the same options YellowPages itself offers
- Filters on minimum rating, minimum review count, years in business, website presence and currently-open status
- Omits any field a listing didn't actually show — no empty strings or nulls in the output

## Output per business

- `businessId` — YellowPages' internal listing ID
- `name`, `businessUrl`
- `website` — the business's own site, when listed
- `phone`
- `categories[]`, `primaryCategory`
- `rating` — 0.5–5.0 stars, only once the business has at least one review
- `reviewCount`, `yearsInBusiness`
- `openStatus` — e.g. "open now", "open 24 hours", "Closed"
- `streetAddress`, `city`, `state`, `zipCode`, `fullAddress`
- `snippet` — short description or review excerpt shown on the results page
- `generalInfo` — longer business description, only with profile enrichment or `businessDetail` mode
- `servicesProducts[]` — listed services or products, only with profile enrichment or `businessDetail` mode
- `hours[]` — `{day, hours}` opening-hours entries, only with profile enrichment or `businessDetail` mode
- `searchLocation` — the location you searched with (`search`/`category` modes)
- `recordType: "business"`, `scrapedAt`

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | `search` | `search`, `category` or `businessDetail` |
| `searchTerms` | string | `restaurants` | What to search for (mode=search); leave blank to list everything at the location |
| `geoLocationTerms` | string | `New York, NY` | City + state or a 5-digit ZIP code (mode=search) |
| `categorySlug` | string | – | YellowPages category slug, e.g. `plumbers` (mode=category) |
| `locationSlug` | string | – | YellowPages location slug, e.g. `new-york-ny` (mode=category) |
| `detailUrls` | array | `[]` | Business profile URLs to fetch directly (mode=businessDetail) |
| `sortBy` | string | `default` | `default`, `distance`, `average_rating` or `name` |
| `fetchBusinessDetails` | boolean | `false` | Visit each business's profile page for hours, description and services (search/category modes); slower |
| `minRating` | string | – | Only keep businesses rated at least this many stars (1–5) |
| `minReviewCount` | integer | – | Only keep businesses with at least this many reviews |
| `minYearsInBusiness` | integer | – | Only keep businesses operating at least this many years |
| `hasWebsiteOnly` | boolean | `false` | Only keep businesses that list a website |
| `openNowOnly` | boolean | `false` | Only keep businesses currently shown as open |
| `maxItems` | integer | `30` | Hard cap on emitted records (1–500) |

### Example: top-rated plumbers in a city

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "searchTerms": "plumbers",
  "geoLocationTerms": "New York, NY",
  "sortBy": "average_rating",
  "minRating": "4",
  "maxItems": 50
}
```

### Example: search by ZIP code, open right now

```json
{
  "mode": "search",
  "searchTerms": "pizza",
  "geoLocationTerms": "10005",
  "openNowOnly": true,
  "maxItems": 30
}
```

### Example: a full category browse with enrichment

```json
{
  "mode": "category",
  "categorySlug": "hair-salons",
  "locationSlug": "los-angeles-ca",
  "fetchBusinessDetails": true,
  "maxItems": 20
}
```

### Example: enrich a known list of profile URLs

```json
{
  "mode": "businessDetail",
  "detailUrls": [
    "https://www.yellowpages.com/new-york-ny/mip/local-plumbing-new-york-ny-550182424"
  ]
}
```

## Use cases

- **Local SEO and marketing agencies** — build a prospect list by category and city
- **Lead generation** — filter on rating, review count and years in business to find established targets
- **Market research** — compare business density and ratings across categories and cities
- **Directory cross-checking** — reconcile a business's YellowPages listing against your own records
- **Competitive tracking** — watch a category's ratings and review counts shift over time
- **Bulk enrichment** — turn a list of known profile URLs into structured contact records

## FAQ

**Is this affiliated with YellowPages.com or YP Holdings?**
No. This is an independent actor that reads publicly available pages on yellowpages.com; it is not affiliated with YP Holdings.

**What's the real difference between `search` and `category` mode?**
`search` matches the YellowPages search box — a free-text keyword plus a city/ZIP, sortable any way YellowPages allows. `category` goes straight to a specific category-and-location browse page when you already know both slugs, skipping the keyword search.

**Why is `rating` missing for some businesses?**
YellowPages only shows a star rating once a business has at least one review; unrated businesses omit the field instead of showing a zero.

**Why are `generalInfo`, `servicesProducts` and `hours` sometimes absent?**
Those fields only come from a business's own profile page. They appear when `fetchBusinessDetails` is on, or always in `businessDetail` mode — leaving enrichment off keeps `search`/`category` runs faster.

**What location formats work?**
`City, ST` (e.g. `Chicago, IL`) or a 5-digit ZIP code (e.g. `60601`); coverage is US-only.

**How current is the listing data?**
Each run reads the live YellowPages page, so results reflect whatever is currently published.

**Why did a heavily filtered search come back empty?**
Combining several filters — minimum rating, minimum reviews and open-now, for example — can legitimately exclude every match in a small result set; try a broader location or fewer filters at once.
